Installed-package list for GTFOBins
examples.command: apt list --installed | tr "/" " " | cut -d" " -f1,3 | sed 's/[0-9]://g' | tee -a installed_pkgs.list

examples.label: Trace syscalls of a helper to find opened paths
OSCP Ch17 — list loaded kernel modules (CVE matching)
OSCP Ch17 — get module version for CVE matching

notes: Root-run services and their config files are prime targets; the installed-package list feeds the GTFOBins cross-reference. strace on a setuid/root helper often leaks paths it opens (hijack candidates). Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Cross-reference the package list against GTFOBins.
Compare service versions against known-vuln list.
Watch for root cron/services with pspy.

name: Enumeration - Services and Internals
description: Dig into running processes, installed packages/binaries, sudo version (for CVEs), config and shell-script files, and live process command lines via /proc.

variations.label: Processes / proc
variations.command:
ps aux | grep root
find /proc -name cmdline -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null | tr " " "\n"
find / -type f \( -name *_hist -o -name *_history \) -exec ls -l {} \; 2>/dev/null

variations.label: Packages / binaries
variations.command:
apt list --installed | tr "/" " " | cut -d" " -f1,3 | sed 's/[0-9]://g' | tee -a installed_pkgs.list
sudo -V
ls -l /bin /usr/bin/ /usr/sbin/

variations.label: Configs / scripts
variations.command:
find / -type f \( -name *.conf -o -name *.config \) -exec ls -l {} \; 2>/dev/null
find / -type f -name "*.sh" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "src\|snap\|share"
strace ping -c1 <ip>
